snippets.title: Overflow and reservoir vent check after overheating
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Coolant loss that appears only after the temperature gauge has climbed past normal during towing or mountain driving is usually coolant pushed out through the overflow. Check the overflow hose routing and the reservoir vent for kinks.

messages.content: Our family's 2017 midsize SUV with the 3.4L V6, just past 43k miles. Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. What test makes sense right now?

Good details, thanks. The first check is this: with the transmission at operating temperature and the engine idling in park on level ground, check the fluid level against the hot range and look at its color and smell [SEC 2.4].
Level is right in the hot range and the fluid looks clean.
Normal there. With the brake held firmly, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine for lift or a gap at any mount [SB 59-983].
No real lift at all going between drive and reverse. So what do you want me to test now?

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. A single-cylinder misfire under load or during acceleration may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with a plug from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Intake runner gasket leak check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. For a single-cylinder misfire code at idle that clears above 1,500 rpm, listen for a vacuum leak at each intake manifold runner with the engine idling and watch fuel trims while you block the suspected runner area. A trim change that follows one runner points to a leaking runner gasket.

messages.content: Fleet unit: 2013 hatchback, 1.6-liter four, 107k miles logged. Misfire code P0304. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. Which check would you run before anything else?

Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SEC 18.1]. Write down the reading so we can compare it to spec.
Seems like overkill. Everyone online says ignition coil.

A part guess could cost you twice. Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SEC 18.1].
Okay, you talked me into it, and here's what I got. Hooked up a spark tester at 25 kV. Strong blue spark every time.

Thanks for checking. Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [SB 85-710].
The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain. I'm about done with checks. Is it time to buy the part?

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: Belt and tensioner check for a battery lamp at cold startup
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. If the battery warning lamp lights for the first minute after a start below 10 deg F, with a short belt squeal that clears once the engine warms, inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. A tensioner that bounces when cold lets the belt slip briefly.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for several days because a control module or accessory circuit does not go to sleep. Close the doors, latch the hood switch closed and let the modules go to sleep, which can take up to 45 minutes. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate the circuit that stays awake by pulling fuses and correct the fault.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

messages.content: Mine is a midsize sedan from 2017, 2.5-liter four under the hood, 163,678 miles so far. At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. Some vehicles may set P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

The automatic slams into second, a hard 1-2 shift, and it's worse once the transmission is fully warmed up. Not sure if it's connected, but CEL came on with P0171. It idles rough at stoplights and stumbles a little right after a cold start, but it pulls fine on the highway. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

snippets.title: Battery drain from infotainment head unit
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. The infotainment head unit may not enter sleep mode after a software update and drain the battery within a few days. Measure parasitic draw and check whether the head unit stays awake. Repair: update the head unit software.

messages.content: Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. Shop ticket: 2016 midsize sedan, 3.5L V6, odometer 131,211. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: With the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Intake runner gasket leak check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. A trim change that follows one runner points to a leaking runner gasket.

messages.content: The check engine light flashes when I accelerate hard or climb hills, and it stored P0301 (cylinder 1 misfire). Idle is smooth, and it does it in dry weather too. Mine is a minivan from 2015, 3.5-liter V6 under the hood, 97k miles so far. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). Harsh engagements and firm shifts may occur when the pressure control solenoid holds line pressure high. Connect a pressure gauge to the line pressure test port. With the engine idling in drive and the brake applied, line pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2014-2020. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Repair: update the transmission control software.

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
snippets.text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes, model years 2012-2015. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points. Repair: replace the rear drums.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

messages.content: Got a 2014 midsize sedan here, 2.5L four-cylinder, around 155,327 miles on it. The battery light flickers at idle and the headlights dim, and they brighten when I rev the engine. It happens warm or cold. Rental car runs out Monday, so I need the repair, not homework.

snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). snippets.title: Flickering lights from a failed alternator diode
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Headlights may flicker or dim at idle because a failed rectifier diode reduces alternator output. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.

snippets.title: Battery monitoring sensor check, auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. On vehicles driven mostly on trips under 10 minutes that show a low battery message, check the battery monitoring sensor data with a scan tool. A sensor that reports a low state of charge limits charging and keeps the battery low.

messages.content: Please keep it simple and just name the bad part. Fleet unit: 2015 midsize sedan, 2.5L, 106k miles logged. Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. Give me your best guess on the part. I won't hold you to it.

snippets.title: Charge air pipe inspection for lean codes under boost
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. When P0171 sets during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal, inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. A pipe that leaks only under boost admits unmetered air at high load.

snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing

messages.content: Fleet unit: 2016 hatchback, 1.6-liter four, 53k miles logged. My air conditioning is blowing warm air from the dash vents on both sides, all the time. The blower is fine. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. A pedal or steering wheel pulsation may develop several thousand miles after a brake or wheel service when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side.

messages.content: I bought a used 2011 midsize sedan with the 3.5-liter V6; it shows 187k miles. At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving.

snippets.title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with a molded lower radiator hose. Coolant temperature may rise during sustained highway driving or towing while temperature in stop-and-go traffic stays normal. Inspect the lower radiator hose for collapse at high rpm with the engine warm. Repair: install the reinforced lower hose.

snippets.title: Rear AC expansion valve check
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2010-2018. When the front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm, compare the front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. A rear outlet line much warmer than the front points to a rear expansion valve stuck closed.

snippets.title: Temperature gauge reads high with normal coolant temperature
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans with the 2.0L I4 engine, model years 2020-2022. The temperature gauge may read high in traffic while actual coolant temperature is normal. Compare the gauge with the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool. Repair: update the instrument cluster software.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2017 compact crossover, 2.4L, odometer 106k. The AC blows warm from every front vent, driver and passenger side alike. It was cold last summer. The blower works on all speeds. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play.

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2013-2020. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. For a clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock.

messages.content: Got a 2013 full-size pickup here, 5.5-liter V8, around 29k miles on it. The front right side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet.

snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor. Some vehicles may set lean codes with high long-term fuel trim at idle because a contaminated sensor element under-reports airflow. With the engine at operating temperature and idling with all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement (about 2-2.5 g/s for a 2.0L engine). Repair: clean the sensor element with an approved cleaner or replace the sensor.

snippets.title: Fuel pressure and hold test, returnless systems
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a fuel rail test port. Key on, engine off, connect a pressure gauge at the rail test port. Specified pressure is 55-62 psi, and it should hold within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off. Low pressure can produce lean codes and a rough idle; low pressure together with high fuel trims at all speeds points to fuel delivery.

With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts. A clunk or pop from the front over bumps or while turning at low speed may come from a worn strut upper mount or mount bearing. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing. Repair: replace the strut upper mounts and bearings.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked.

messages.content: Misfire code P0303. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. Hi. 2015 hatchback, 1.6L engine, roughly 161,767 on the odometer. What should I test to start narrowing it down?

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. For a clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play.

messages.content: Hi. 2017 compact crossover, 2.4L four-cylinder engine, roughly 74k on the odometer. Clunk from the front end, right side, on rough pavement. It definitely comes from the front, and it doesn't happen when turning sharply. I've already lost two weekends on this. What's the part?

snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If the engine turns over noticeably slower when hot than when cold, measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp while cranking with fuel disabled. Draw above 250 A on a four- or six-cylinder engine indicates excessive starter load. This procedure covers slow crank speed only, not an engine that cranks at normal speed but is slow to fire.

snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor. Some vehicles may set lean codes with high long-term fuel trim at idle because a contaminated sensor element under-reports airflow. With the engine at operating temperature and idling with all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement (about 2-2.5 g/s for a 2.0L engine). Repair: clean the sensor element with an approved cleaner or replace the sensor.

snippets.title: Fuel pump relay check for delayed prime
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. If restarts are delayed after towing or extended idling in hot weather, check the fuel pump relay terminals for discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Pressure that rises slowly on a hot restart points to worn relay contacts delaying pump prime.

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2013-2020. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side.

snippets.title: Belt and tensioner check for a battery lamp at cold startup
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. If the battery warning lamp lights for the first minute after a start below 10 deg F, with a short belt squeal that clears once the engine warms, inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. A tensioner that bounces when cold lets the belt slip briefly.

snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). Harsh engagements and firm shifts may occur when the pressure control solenoid holds line pressure high. Connect a pressure gauge to the line pressure test port. With the engine idling in drive and the brake applied, line pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

Drive until the engine is at full operating temperature, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and record the pressure 20 minutes later. Pressure should stay above 30 psi. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake

snippets.title: Fuel pressure and hold test, returnless systems
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a fuel rail test port. Key on, engine off, connect a pressure gauge at the rail test port. Specified pressure is 55-62 psi, and it should hold within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off. Low pressure can produce lean codes and a rough idle; low pressure together with high fuel trims at all speeds points to fuel delivery.

snippets.title: Rear AC expansion valve check
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2010-2018. When the front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm, compare the front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. A rear outlet line much warmer than the front points to a rear expansion valve stuck closed.

messages.content: Not looking for a troubleshooting tree here. Daily driver is a 2012 compact sedan (2.0L four-cylinder) with 84k miles. Check engine light is on with P0171 (system too lean, bank 1). The idle is rough, worst for the first few minutes after a cold start. I'd rather throw a mass airflow sensor at it than spend a weekend testing.

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: With the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. Some vehicles may set P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

snippets.title: Intake runner gasket leak check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. For a single-cylinder misfire code at idle that clears above 1,500 rpm, listen for a vacuum leak at each intake manifold runner with the engine idling and watch fuel trims while you block the suspected runner area. A trim change that follows one runner points to a leaking runner gasket.

messages.content: Our family's 2010 compact sedan with the 1.8L, just past 90k miles. Misfire code P0301. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter.

snippets.title: Fuel pump relay check for delayed prime
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. If restarts are delayed after towing or extended idling in hot weather, check the fuel pump relay terminals for discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Pressure that rises slowly on a hot restart points to worn relay contacts delaying pump prime.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from intake manifold gasket shrinkage
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with the revised composite intake manifold. P0171 may set at idle after a cold soak because the manifold-to-head gasket shrinks at low temperature. Smoke-test the intake with the engine cold, concentrating on the manifold-to-head joint. Repair: replace the intake manifold gasket with the updated part.

snippets.title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. P0171 may set only during steady cruise above 50 mph on a fully warm engine; idle quality is normal and the code does not set at idle. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Repair: replace the purge valve.

snippets.title: Charge air pipe inspection for lean codes under boost
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. When P0171 sets during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal, inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. A pipe that leaks only under boost admits unmetered air at high load.

messages.content: I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm. Our family's 2019 full-size pickup with the 5.5L V8, just past 51k miles. What should I test to start narrowing it down?

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to all models. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side.

snippets.title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with a molded lower radiator hose. Coolant temperature may rise during sustained highway driving or towing while temperature in stop-and-go traffic stays normal. Inspect the lower radiator hose for collapse at high rpm with the engine warm. Repair: install the reinforced lower hose.

snippets.title: Turbocharger coolant line inspection
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. With the engine cold, inspect the turbocharger coolant return line fitting and the line for dried coolant residue. Residue at the fitting accounts for slow coolant loss with no drips under the vehicle.

snippets.title: Intake runner gasket leak check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. A trim change that follows one runner points to a leaking runner gasket.

snippets.title: Belt and tensioner check for a battery lamp at cold startup
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. If the battery warning lamp lights for the first minute after a start below 10 deg F, with a short belt squeal that clears once the engine warms, inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. A tensioner that bounces when cold lets the belt slip briefly.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for several days because a control module or accessory circuit does not go to sleep. Close the doors, latch the hood switch closed and let the modules go to sleep, which can take up to 45 minutes. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate the circuit that stays awake by pulling fuses and correct the fault.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts. A clunk or pop from the front over bumps or while turning at low speed may come from a worn strut upper mount or mount bearing. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing. Repair: replace the strut upper mounts and bearings.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic when scale or debris restricts flow through the radiator core. With the engine at operating temperature and the thermostat open, use an infrared thermometer to compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: replace the radiator and flush the cooling system.

snippets.title: Viscous fan clutch check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines with an engine-driven fan, model years 2013-2020. With the engine off and cool, spin the fan by hand: it should turn no more than about one revolution. A fan clutch that freewheels lets temperature climb at idle and in slow traffic.

messages.content: Please keep it simple and just name the bad part. Got a 2013 minivan here, 3.5-liter V6, around 113k miles on it. snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side.

messages.content: Got a 2010 compact sedan here, 1.8-liter engine, around 108k miles on it. The brake pedal pulses and the steering wheel shakes when I brake from highway speed on dry pavement. It's smooth when I'm not braking. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Overflow and reservoir vent check after overheating
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Coolant loss that appears only after the temperature gauge has climbed past normal during towing or mountain driving is usually coolant pushed out through the overflow. Check the overflow hose routing and the reservoir vent for kinks.

snippets.title: Coolant loss with no visible leak from an early-venting cap
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. The coolant level may drop slowly with no visible leak or puddle because the pressure cap vents early and coolant escapes through the overflow as vapor. Fit the radiator or reservoir cap to a cap adapter on the pressure tester and pump until the cap vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with coil-on-plug ignition. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. A pedal or steering wheel pulsation may develop several thousand miles after a brake or wheel service when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). Harsh engagements and firm shifts may occur when the pressure control solenoid holds line pressure high. Connect a pressure gauge to the line pressure test port. With the engine idling in drive and the brake applied, line pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Flickering lights from a failed alternator diode
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Headlights may flicker or dim at idle because a failed rectifier diode reduces alternator output. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.

snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed.

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2013-2020. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock.

snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. A long crank may occur on restarts after a short stop with a hot engine because rail pressure bleeds down and fuel boils in the hot rail. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans (not the 5.5L V8). Coolant temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic while it stays normal at highway speed if the radiator fan does not run. With the engine at operating temperature and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold gasket
snippets.text: Applies to 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2020-2022. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at a coolant passage. Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the gasket area with a borescope through the throttle body opening. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

snippets.title: Overflow and reservoir vent check after overheating
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Coolant loss that appears only after the temperature gauge has climbed past normal during towing or mountain driving is usually coolant pushed out through the overflow. Check the overflow hose routing and the reservoir vent for kinks.

snippets.title: Turbocharger coolant line inspection
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. With the engine cold, inspect the turbocharger coolant return line fitting and the line for dried coolant residue. Residue at the fitting accounts for slow coolant loss with no drips under the vehicle.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic when scale or debris restricts flow through the radiator core. With the engine at operating temperature and the thermostat open, use an infrared thermometer to compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: replace the radiator and flush the cooling system.

snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check

snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines with a belt-driven alternator, model years 2010-2020. snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed.

snippets.title: CVT fluid and software level check for judder
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. For a judder or shudder during light acceleration from 15-35 mph, check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Degraded fluid or an early software level causes judder at light throttle.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check

Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts. A clunk or pop from the front over bumps or while turning at low speed may come from a worn strut upper mount or mount bearing. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing. Repair: replace the strut upper mounts and bearings.

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

messages.content: Mine is a compact sedan from 2012, 1.8-liter engine under the hood, 156k miles so far. Okay, you talked me into it, and here's what I got. Hooked up a spark tester at 25 kV. Strong blue spark every time.

snippets.title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed

Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to all models. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side.

snippets.title: Rear AC expansion valve check
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2010-2018. When the front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm, compare the front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. A rear outlet line much warmer than the front points to a rear expansion valve stuck closed.

snippets.title: Warm AC at idle from an inoperative condenser fan
snippets.text: Applies to models with an electric condenser fan. Vent air may warm up at idle and in traffic and cool again at speed when the condenser fan does not run. With the engine idling and the AC switched on, confirm the condenser fan runs. Without airflow across the condenser at idle, high-side pressure rises. Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.

messages.content: Hi. 2013 midsize sedan, 3.5-liter V6 engine, roughly 42k on the odometer. The AC blows warm from every front vent, driver and passenger side alike. It was cold last summer. The blower works on all speeds. Any idea which check to begin with?
With the engine running, the AC on max and the blower on high, watch whether the compressor clutch plate pulls in and spins with the pulley [TSB-9603]. Let me know what you find.
The clutch pulls in and stays engaged, spinning with the pulley.
Good, that clears this area. With the engine idling and the AC on, confirm the condenser fan is running [SM-4809].
The condenser fan comes on as soon as the AC is on. What would you look at following that result?

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2013-2020. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after a few days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery.

messages.content: Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link.

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: With the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Wheel speed sensor tone ring inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed.

snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits

A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

messages.content: Not looking for a troubleshooting tree here. Mine is a hatchback from 2016, 1.6L four-cylinder under the hood, 41k miles so far. snippets.title: Dim lights at idle from a slipping accessory belt
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines with a belt-driven alternator, model years 2010-2020. snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: CVT fluid and software level check for judder

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Some vehicles may crank for several seconds before starting on a hot restart because the engine is overfueled. If the engine starts noticeably faster in clear-flood mode, it is being overfueled on hot restarts. Repair: correct the overfueling source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic when scale or debris restricts flow through the radiator core. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: replace the radiator and flush the cooling system.

snippets.title: Turbocharger coolant line inspection
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. With the engine cold, inspect the turbocharger coolant return line fitting and the line for dried coolant residue. Residue at the fitting accounts for slow coolant loss with no drips under the vehicle.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan

Coolant temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic while it stays normal at highway speed if the radiator fan does not run. With the engine at operating temperature and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

messages.content: The battery light flickers at idle and the headlights dim, and they brighten when I rev the engine. It happens warm or cold. Our family's 2015 compact crossover with the 2.4L four-cylinder, just past 95,237 miles. Honestly I just want a part number so I can order tonight.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. A pedal or steering wheel pulsation may develop several thousand miles after a brake or wheel service when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2018 midsize SUV (3.4L V6) with 67k miles. Check engine light is on with P0171 (system too lean, bank 1). The idle is rough, worst for the first few minutes after a cold start. One more thing: shimmy in the steering wheel only when braking from 60 mph or so. Light stops around town on smooth roads are fine. The sun visor on my side won't stay up. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from intake manifold gasket shrinkage
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with the revised composite intake manifold. P0171 may set at idle after a cold soak because the manifold-to-head gasket shrinks at low temperature. Smoke-test the intake with the engine cold, concentrating on the manifold-to-head joint. Repair: replace the intake manifold gasket with the updated part.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. For a clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock.

messages.content: This is my 2018 midsize sedan. It has the 3.5-liter V6 and about 77,964 miles. There's a clunk from the front left when I go over speed bumps or potholes at low speed, driving straight. Nothing when I turn the wheel in a parking lot. Besides that, P0171 keeps coming back a day after I clear it. The idle shakes the steering wheel a bit when it's cold, and the freeze frame says it set at idle. I'd like to diagnose it properly. snippets.title: Charge air pipe inspection for lean codes under boost
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. When P0171 sets during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal, inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. A pipe that leaks only under boost admits unmetered air at high load.

snippets.title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. P0171 may set only during steady cruise above 50 mph on a fully warm engine; idle quality is normal and the code does not set at idle. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Repair: replace the purge valve.

snippets.title: Fuel pressure and hold test, returnless systems
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a fuel rail test port. Key on, engine off, connect a pressure gauge at the rail test port. Specified pressure is 55-62 psi, and it should hold within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off. Low pressure can produce lean codes and a rough idle; low pressure together with high fuel trims at all speeds points to fuel delivery.

messages.content: Mine is a compact sedan from 2018, 2.0-liter four under the hood, 138,320 miles so far. I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2018 full-size pickup (5.5-liter V8) with 43,924 miles. CEL came on with P0171. It idles rough at stoplights and stumbles a little right after a cold start, but it pulls fine on the highway.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

messages.content: Misfire code P0304. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. I bought a used 2017 midsize SUV with the 3.4L V6; it shows 53k miles. I've already lost two weekends on this. What's the part?

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output.

snippets.title: Dim lights at idle from a slipping accessory belt
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines with a belt-driven alternator, model years 2010-2020. Lights may dim at idle under electrical load because a glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip. With the engine off, inspect the accessory drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. Repair: replace the belt and tensioner.

Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2018 compact sedan, 2.0L, odometer 179,933. Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. messages.content: The automatic slams into second, a hard 1-2 shift, and it's worse once the transmission is fully warmed up. Shop ticket: 2018 midsize sedan, 3.5-liter V6, odometer 52,264. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after a few days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery.

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

messages.content: Our family's 2020 midsize sedan with the 2.5-liter four, just past 55k miles. Shimmy in the steering wheel only when braking from 60 mph or so. Light stops around town on smooth roads are fine. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. Fit the radiator or reservoir cap to a cap adapter on the pressure tester and pump until the cap vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

snippets.text: Applies to 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2020-2022. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at a coolant passage. snippets.text: Applies to all models. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. If the engine starts noticeably faster in clear-flood mode, it is being overfueled on hot restarts. Repair: correct the overfueling source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

messages.content: Got a 2018 hatchback here, 1.6-liter four, around 59k miles on it. The battery light comes on now and then at idle with the lights and blower on, and the headlights look dim. Revving it makes the light go out. Outside temperature doesn't matter. What test makes sense right now?

messages.content: Mine is a midsize sedan from 2013, 3.5L V6 under the hood, 58,959 miles so far. The AC blows warm from every front vent, driver and passenger side alike. It was cold last summer. The blower works on all speeds. I'd rather throw a AC clutch at it than spend a weekend testing.

snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for several days because a control module or accessory circuit does not go to sleep. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate the circuit that stays awake by pulling fuses and correct the fault.

snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2020 small crossover, 1.4-liter turbo, odometer 89,914. Misfire code P0304. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter.

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts. A clunk or pop from the front over bumps or while turning at low speed may come from a worn strut upper mount or mount bearing. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing. Repair: replace the strut upper mounts and bearings.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2015 minivan (3.5-liter V6) with 87,829 miles. The battery light comes on now and then at idle with the lights and blower on, and the headlights look dim. Revving it makes the light go out. Outside temperature doesn't matter. I'm leaning toward a new alternator. Talk me out of it or tell me to go ahead.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: CVT fluid and software level check for judder
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. For a judder or shudder during light acceleration from 15-35 mph, check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Degraded fluid or an early software level causes judder at light throttle.

messages.content: I bought a used 2019 compact sedan with the 2.0L four-cylinder; it shows 90,811 miles. Hard, delayed shifts once the car is warm. The first few miles cold are actually smoother. How would you approach this first?

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Fuel pressure and hold test, returnless systems
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a fuel rail test port. Key on, engine off, connect a pressure gauge at the rail test port. Specified pressure is 55-62 psi, and it should hold within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off. Low pressure can produce lean codes and a rough idle; low pressure together with high fuel trims at all speeds points to fuel delivery.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. A pedal or steering wheel pulsation may develop several thousand miles after a brake or wheel service when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

messages.content: This is my 2016 hatchback. It has the 1.6-liter four and about 66,734 miles. I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm. Not sure if it's connected, but pedal pulsation when slowing down from highway speed, felt mostly through the steering wheel rather than the seat. No vibration while cruising, and I'm not towing anything. The fuel door sometimes won't pop open. How would you approach this first?

snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If the engine turns over noticeably slower when hot than when cold, measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp while cranking with fuel disabled. Draw above 250 A on a four- or six-cylinder engine indicates excessive starter load. This procedure covers slow crank speed only, not an engine that cranks at normal speed but is slow to fire.

snippets.title: Fuel pump relay check for delayed prime
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. If restarts are delayed after towing or extended idling in hot weather, check the fuel pump relay terminals for discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Pressure that rises slowly on a hot restart points to worn relay contacts delaying pump prime.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

messages.content: When I stop for 15 to 30 minutes after driving, it cranks at normal speed for five or six seconds before it fires. Cold starts in the morning are instant. Fleet unit: 2017 small crossover, 1.4L turbo, 175k miles logged. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Overflow and reservoir vent check after overheating
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Coolant loss that appears only after the temperature gauge has climbed past normal during towing or mountain driving is usually coolant pushed out through the overflow. Check the overflow hose routing and the reservoir vent for kinks.

snippets.title: Turbocharger coolant line inspection
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. With the engine cold, inspect the turbocharger coolant return line fitting and the line for dried coolant residue. Residue at the fitting accounts for slow coolant loss with no drips under the vehicle.

snippets.title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold gasket
snippets.text: Applies to 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2020-2022. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at a coolant passage. Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the gasket area with a borescope through the throttle body opening. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans (not the 5.5L V8). Coolant temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic while it stays normal at highway speed if the radiator fan does not run. With the engine at operating temperature and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

messages.content: Coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. No drips on the driveway, no steam, and the temp gauge stays normal. Mine is a compact sedan from 2017, 2.0-liter four under the hood, 114k miles so far. What's a sensible first test here?

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to all models. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side.

snippets.title: Warm AC at idle from an inoperative condenser fan
snippets.text: Applies to models with an electric condenser fan. Vent air may warm up at idle and in traffic and cool again at speed when the condenser fan does not run. With the engine idling and the AC switched on, confirm the condenser fan runs. Without airflow across the condenser at idle, high-side pressure rises. Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Rear AC expansion valve check
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2010-2018. When the front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm, compare the front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. A rear outlet line much warmer than the front points to a rear expansion valve stuck closed.

snippets.title: Dim lights at idle from a slipping accessory belt
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines with a belt-driven alternator, model years 2010-2020. Lights may dim at idle under electrical load because a glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip. With the engine off, inspect the accessory drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. Repair: replace the belt and tensioner.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2013-2020. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2015 hatchback, 1.6L four-cylinder, odometer 106,733. At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving. What test makes sense right now?
