snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

messages.content: Mine is a midsize SUV from 2013, 3.4-liter V6 under the hood, 122,547 miles so far. There's a clunk from the front right when I go over speed bumps or potholes at low speed, driving straight. Nothing when I turn the wheel in a parking lot. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Rear AC expansion valve check
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2010-2018. When the front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm, compare the front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. A rear outlet line much warmer than the front points to a rear expansion valve stuck closed.

snippets.title: Temperature gauge reads high with normal coolant temperature
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans with the 2.0L I4 engine, model years 2020-2022. The temperature gauge may read high in traffic while actual coolant temperature is normal. Compare the gauge with the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool. Repair: update the instrument cluster software.

messages.content: My air conditioning is blowing warm air from the dash vents on both sides, all the time. The blower is fine. Hi. 2012 hatchback, 1.6L four-cylinder engine, roughly 174,014 on the odometer. Skip the explanation. Is the AC clutch the thing to buy?

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: Battery drain from infotainment head unit
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. The infotainment head unit may not enter sleep mode after a software update and drain the battery within a few days. Measure parasitic draw and check whether the head unit stays awake. Repair: update the head unit software.

messages.content: The battery light comes on now and then at idle with the lights and blower on, and the headlights look dim. Revving it makes the light go out. Outside temperature doesn't matter. Fleet unit: 2015 midsize sedan, 3.5-liter V6, 42k miles logged. What's a sensible first test here?

snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines with an engine-driven fan, model years 2013-2020. With the engine off and cool, spin the fan by hand: it should turn no more than about one revolution. A fan clutch that freewheels lets temperature climb at idle and in slow traffic.

snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor

Repair: clean the sensor element with an approved cleaner or replace the sensor.

messages.content: When I stop for 15 to 30 minutes after driving, it cranks at normal speed for five or six seconds before it fires. Cold starts in the morning are instant. Our family's 2013 compact sedan with the 2.0L four-cylinder, just past 167,245 miles.

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Wheel speed sensor tone ring inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed.

snippets.title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with a molded lower radiator hose. Coolant temperature may rise during sustained highway driving or towing while temperature in stop-and-go traffic stays normal. Inspect the lower radiator hose for collapse at high rpm with the engine warm. Repair: install the reinforced lower hose.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic when scale or debris restricts flow through the radiator core. With the engine at operating temperature and the thermostat open, use an infrared thermometer to compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: replace the radiator and flush the cooling system.

snippets.title: Temperature gauge reads high with normal coolant temperature

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test

Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
snippets.text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes, model years 2012-2015. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points. Repair: replace the rear drums.

snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from fuel pressure bleed-down
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. A long crank may occur on restarts after a short stop with a hot engine because rail pressure bleeds down and fuel boils in the hot rail. Fit the radiator or reservoir cap to a cap adapter on the pressure tester and pump until the cap vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

messages.content: Please keep it simple and just name the bad part. Our family's 2014 compact crossover with the 2.4L four-cylinder, just past 183,013 miles. Coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. No drips on the driveway, no steam, and the temp gauge stays normal. A guy at work swears it's the radiator. I'm inclined to just buy it.

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link.

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to all models. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side.

messages.content: The AC isn't cooling anymore. Air from all the front vents, both sides, is barely cooler than outside, from the moment I start it. Fan speeds all work. Hi. 2019 full-size pickup, 5.5L V8 engine, roughly 78,364 on the odometer. How would you approach this first?

snippets.title: Wheel speed sensor tone ring inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed.

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
snippets.text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes, model years 2012-2015. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points. Repair: replace the rear drums.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. A pedal or steering wheel pulsation may develop several thousand miles after a brake or wheel service when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

snippets.title: Charge air pipe inspection for lean codes under boost
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. When P0171 sets during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal, inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. A pipe that leaks only under boost admits unmetered air at high load.

messages.content: Got a 2017 midsize SUV here, 3.4L V6, around 74k miles on it. Pedal pulsation when slowing down from highway speed, felt mostly through the steering wheel rather than the seat. No vibration while cruising, and I'm not towing anything. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: Intake runner gasket leak check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. For a single-cylinder misfire code at idle that clears above 1,500 rpm, listen for a vacuum leak at each intake manifold runner with the engine idling and watch fuel trims while you block the suspected runner area. A trim change that follows one runner points to a leaking runner gasket.

snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with coil-on-plug ignition. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. Some vehicles may set P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: With the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

messages.content: Fleet unit: 2013 compact sedan, 2.0L, 150k miles logged. It bucks under load, like merging onto the highway, and the scan tool shows P0303. No problem at idle, rain or shine. What should I test to start narrowing it down?

snippets.title: Warm AC after restart from electric compressor inverter
snippets.text: Applies to small crossovers with an electric AC compressor, model years 2022-2024. The AC may blow warm for several minutes after a restart because the compressor inverter is slow to initialize. Read compressor inverter codes with a scan tool. Repair: update the compressor inverter software.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

messages.content: Got a 2017 full-size pickup here, 5.5L V8, around 164k miles on it. The check engine light flashes when I accelerate hard or climb hills, and it stored P0303 (cylinder 3 misfire). Idle is smooth, and it does it in dry weather too. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans (not the 5.5L V8). Coolant temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic while it stays normal at highway speed if the radiator fan does not run. With the engine at operating temperature and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic when scale or debris restricts flow through the radiator core. With the engine at operating temperature and the thermostat open, use an infrared thermometer to compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: replace the radiator and flush the cooling system.

messages.content: Got a 2019 midsize sedan here, 2.5L, around 73k miles on it. Got stuck in a drive-through line and the temp gauge went almost to the red. Once I got back on the road it came down. It never runs hot at highway speed. Any idea which check to begin with?
Good details, thanks. The first check is this: with the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool and confirm the fan starts [SM 2.1.7].
Just finished that. Commanded the fan with my scanner and it spun up on both speeds.
Good, that clears this area. With the engine cold, open the radiator or degas bottle cap and look at whether coolant is right up to the neck or the cold-fill line [SM 8.3.7].
Level is at the cold-fill line, nothing low. Which test makes sense now that this one came back fine?

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Combustion leak (block) test
snippets.text: With the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself.

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums

Fit the radiator or reservoir cap to a cap adapter on the pressure tester and pump until the cap vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

messages.content: Got a 2012 compact sedan here, 1.8L four-cylinder, around 25k miles on it. Coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. No drips on the driveway, no steam, and the temp gauge stays normal. What should I test to start narrowing it down?

Begin here: with the engine cold, pressurize the cooling system to the cap rating and watch for a pressure drop over 15 minutes while you inspect the hoses, water pump weep hole and radiator tanks [SEC 12.22].
Here's what I found. It held 16 psi for fifteen minutes with no wet spots anywhere.
Thanks for checking. Test the radiator or reservoir cap on a cap adapter and confirm it holds at least its stamped pressure rating [SB 47-902].
The cap held its rated 16 psi on the adapter. Which test makes sense now that this one came back fine?

snippets.title: Cold-weather cranking capacity check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If a battery that is healthy in mild weather does not crank the engine after sitting overnight below 0 deg F, with no parasitic draw present, compare the battery's cold cranking rating with the engine requirement and check whether a block heater is fitted and used. This check covers cold-soak no-starts only.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

snippets.title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts. A clunk or pop from the front over bumps or while turning at low speed may come from a worn strut upper mount or mount bearing. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing. Repair: replace the strut upper mounts and bearings.

snippets.title: Battery drain from infotainment head unit
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. The infotainment head unit may not enter sleep mode after a software update and drain the battery within a few days. Measure parasitic draw and check whether the head unit stays awake. Repair: update the head unit software.

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after a few days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for several days because a control module or accessory circuit does not go to sleep. Close the doors, latch the hood switch closed and let the modules go to sleep, which can take up to 45 minutes. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate the circuit that stays awake by pulling fuses and correct the fault.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked.

messages.content: This is my 2015 midsize sedan. It has the 2.5L and about 78k miles. The battery keeps going flat over a long weekend. Once it's jumped it starts every day as long as I drive it daily. No warning lights while driving, and it isn't cold out. How would you approach this first?

After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V [SB 51-394]. Write down the reading so we can compare it to spec.
Do I really have to test it? I'd rather just buy the alternator.

Ordering parts without a test risks money on the wrong one. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V [SB 51-394].
Okay, you talked me into it, and here's what I got. After the drive it showed 14.2 V at the battery with the lights and blower on.
Good, that clears this area. Fully charge the battery, let it rest, and run a conductance or load test against the CCA rating on its label [SM-8601].
Charged it overnight and the tester says 680 CCA against a 700 rating. It passed. I'm about done with checks. Is it time to buy the part?

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Some vehicles may crank for several seconds before starting on a hot restart because the engine is overfueled. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. If the engine starts noticeably faster in clear-flood mode, it is being overfueled on hot restarts. Repair: correct the overfueling source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

snippets.title: Warm AC at idle from an inoperative condenser fan
snippets.text: Applies to models with an electric condenser fan. Vent air may warm up at idle and in traffic and cool again at speed when the condenser fan does not run. With the engine idling and the AC switched on, confirm the condenser fan runs. Without airflow across the condenser at idle, high-side pressure rises. Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.

messages.content: I bought a used 2011 compact sedan with the 1.8L four-cylinder; it shows 176,483 miles. Hot restarts are the problem. After a short stop at the store it cranks at normal speed but takes forever to catch. First start of the day is fine.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. A single-cylinder misfire under load or during acceleration may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with a plug from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

This check covers cold-soak no-starts only.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

messages.content: Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. Shop ticket: 2015 midsize sedan, 3.5-liter V6, odometer 120,439. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock.

snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans with the 2.0L I4 engine, model years 2020-2022. The temperature gauge may read high in traffic while actual coolant temperature is normal. Compare the gauge with the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool. Repair: update the instrument cluster software.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check

Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with coil-on-plug ignition. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2016 minivan (3.5L V6) with 96,495 miles. My air conditioning is blowing warm air from the dash vents on both sides, all the time. The blower is fine. And while I'm at it, the check engine light flashes when I accelerate hard or climb hills, and it stored P0302 (cylinder 2 misfire). Idle is smooth, and it does it in dry weather too. What's a sensible first test here?

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after a few days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed.

messages.content: I bought a used 2014 minivan with the 3.5L V6; it shows 66k miles. The battery keeps going flat over a long weekend. Once it's jumped it starts every day as long as I drive it daily. No warning lights while driving, and it isn't cold out. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: Warm AC at idle from an inoperative condenser fan
snippets.text: Applies to models with an electric condenser fan. Vent air may warm up at idle and in traffic and cool again at speed when the condenser fan does not run. With the engine idling and the AC switched on, confirm the condenser fan runs. Without airflow across the condenser at idle, high-side pressure rises. Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

messages.content: This is my 2015 hatchback. It has the 1.6L four-cylinder and about 39,385 miles. My air conditioning is blowing warm air from the dash vents on both sides, all the time. The blower is fine. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. A single-cylinder misfire under load or during acceleration may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with a plug from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Belt and tensioner check for a battery lamp at cold startup
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. If the battery warning lamp lights for the first minute after a start below 10 deg F, with a short belt squeal that clears once the engine warms, inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. A tensioner that bounces when cold lets the belt slip briefly.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play.

messages.content: Hi. 2018 minivan, 3.5L V6 engine, roughly 148,984 on the odometer. The check engine light flashes when I accelerate hard or climb hills, and it stored P0302 (cylinder 2 misfire). Idle is smooth, and it does it in dry weather too. And while I'm at it, the battery light flickers at idle and the headlights dim, and they brighten when I rev the engine. It happens warm or cold. What's a sensible first test here?

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2013-2020. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

messages.content: Clunk from the front end, left side, on rough pavement. It definitely comes from the front, and it doesn't happen when turning sharply. Shop ticket: 2014 compact sedan, 1.8L four-cylinder, odometer 47,643. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: With the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from fuel pressure bleed-down
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. A long crank may occur on restarts after a short stop with a hot engine because rail pressure bleeds down and fuel boils in the hot rail. Drive until the engine is at full operating temperature, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and record the pressure 20 minutes later. Pressure should stay above 30 psi. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). Harsh engagements and firm shifts may occur when the pressure control solenoid holds line pressure high. Connect a pressure gauge to the line pressure test port. With the engine idling in drive and the brake applied, line pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Some vehicles may crank for several seconds before starting on a hot restart because the engine is overfueled. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. If the engine starts noticeably faster in clear-flood mode, it is being overfueled on hot restarts. Repair: correct the overfueling source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

messages.content: This is my 2016 compact sedan. It has the 1.8L and about 186,056 miles. Hot restarts are the problem. After a short stop at the store it cranks at normal speed but takes forever to catch. First start of the day is fine. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

Good details, thanks. The first check is this: drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the fuel rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later; it should still be above 30 psi [TSB-3830].
Just finished that. Residual pressure held at about 40 psi twenty minutes after shutdown.

Normal there. With the engine fully warm, compare the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading at the thermostat housing; they should agree within 10 deg F [SM-0496].
Scan tool said 201 and the infrared gun said 196 at the housing. Nothing showed up, so I'm guessing it's the starter. Agree?

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to all models. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side.

snippets.title: Wheel speed sensor tone ring inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2018 minivan, 3.5-liter V6, odometer 85,275. The AC isn't cooling anymore. Air from all the front vents, both sides, is barely cooler than outside, from the moment I start it. Fan speeds all work. And while I'm at it, pedal pulsation when slowing down from highway speed, felt mostly through the steering wheel rather than the seat. No vibration while cruising, and I'm not towing anything.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2014-2020. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Repair: update the transmission control software.

messages.content: Our family's 2019 compact sedan with the 2.0L four-cylinder, just past 87k miles. The AC isn't cooling anymore. Air from all the front vents, both sides, is barely cooler than outside, from the moment I start it. Fan speeds all work. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. For a clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock.

messages.content: Mine is a midsize sedan from 2013, 2.5-liter four under the hood, 175k miles so far. There's a clunk from the front right when I go over speed bumps or potholes at low speed, driving straight. Nothing when I turn the wheel in a parking lot. I'm leaning toward a new sway bar link. Talk me out of it or tell me to go ahead.

snippets.title: Turbocharger coolant line inspection
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. With the engine cold, inspect the turbocharger coolant return line fitting and the line for dried coolant residue. Residue at the fitting accounts for slow coolant loss with no drips under the vehicle.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

messages.content: Mine is a midsize sedan from 2014, 2.5L four-cylinder under the hood, 182,713 miles so far. Shimmy in the steering wheel only when braking from 60 mph or so. Light stops around town on smooth roads are fine. Not sure if it's connected, but I have to top off the coolant reservoir every week or two. There are no puddles under the car and it has never overheated.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

snippets.title: Battery monitoring sensor check, auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. On vehicles driven mostly on trips under 10 minutes that show a low battery message, check the battery monitoring sensor data with a scan tool. A sensor that reports a low state of charge limits charging and keeps the battery low.

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

messages.content: Got a 2016 midsize sedan here, 3.5L V6, around 145k miles on it. Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. What should I test to start narrowing it down?

snippets.title: Charge air pipe inspection for lean codes under boost
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. When P0171 sets during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal, inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. A pipe that leaks only under boost admits unmetered air at high load.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

messages.content: Mine is a compact sedan from 2013, 2.0L under the hood, 143k miles so far. Check engine light is on with P0171 (system too lean, bank 1). The idle is rough, worst for the first few minutes after a cold start. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

snippets.title: Warm AC after restart from electric compressor inverter
snippets.text: Applies to small crossovers with an electric AC compressor, model years 2022-2024. The AC may blow warm for several minutes after a restart because the compressor inverter is slow to initialize. Read compressor inverter codes with a scan tool. Repair: update the compressor inverter software.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. P0171 may set only during steady cruise above 50 mph on a fully warm engine; idle quality is normal and the code does not set at idle. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Repair: replace the purge valve.

messages.content: Fleet unit: 2011 compact sedan, 1.8L four-cylinder, 94,376 miles logged. I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm. Honestly I just want a part number so I can order tonight.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: CVT fluid and software level check for judder
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. For a judder or shudder during light acceleration from 15-35 mph, check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Degraded fluid or an early software level causes judder at light throttle.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2015 midsize sedan, 3.5-liter V6, odometer 92k. Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. What's a sensible first test here?
Begin here: with the brake held firmly, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine for lift or a gap at any mount [SEC 10.28].
Here's what I found. The engine barely moves when shifting and the mounts look intact.

That result clears it. With the transmission at operating temperature and the engine idling in park on level ground, check the fluid level against the hot range and look at its color and smell [SEC 5.13].
Level is right in the hot range and the fluid looks clean. I've run out of patience with testing. Which part do I order?

snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Repair: replace the purge valve.

snippets.title: Charge air pipe inspection for lean codes under boost
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. A pipe that leaks only under boost admits unmetered air at high load.

snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor. Some vehicles may set lean codes with high long-term fuel trim at idle because a contaminated sensor element under-reports airflow. With the engine at operating temperature and idling with all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement (about 2-2.5 g/s for a 2.0L engine). Repair: clean the sensor element with an approved cleaner or replace the sensor.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

messages.content: Check engine light is on with P0171 (system too lean, bank 1). The idle is rough, worst for the first few minutes after a cold start. I bought a used 2018 midsize sedan with the 2.5L four-cylinder; it shows 135,376 miles. What's a sensible first test here?

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
snippets.text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes, model years 2012-2015. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points. Repair: replace the rear drums.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans (not the 5.5L V8). Coolant temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic while it stays normal at highway speed if the radiator fan does not run. With the engine at operating temperature and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

Light stops around town on smooth roads are fine. snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with coil-on-plug ignition. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

messages.content: Our family's 2015 midsize sedan with the 3.5L V6, just past 163k miles. It bucks under load, like merging onto the highway, and the scan tool shows P0301. No problem at idle, rain or shine. How would you approach this first?

Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SM-0418]. Write down the reading so we can compare it to spec.
Checked it. The spark tester showed a solid blue spark the whole time I cranked it.

Good, that clears this area. Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [SB 13-518].
The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain. Where should I go with this from here?

snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. For a clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock.

snippets.title: Intake runner gasket leak check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. A trim change that follows one runner points to a leaking runner gasket.

snippets.title: Viscous fan clutch check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines with an engine-driven fan, model years 2013-2020. With the engine off and cool, spin the fan by hand: it should turn no more than about one revolution. A fan clutch that freewheels lets temperature climb at idle and in slow traffic.

snippets.title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold gasket
snippets.text: Applies to 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2020-2022. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at a coolant passage. Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the gasket area with a borescope through the throttle body opening. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. A pedal or steering wheel pulsation may develop several thousand miles after a brake or wheel service when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts

A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after a few days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery.

messages.content: Misfire code P0304. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. Hi. 2014 hatchback, 1.6L four-cylinder engine, roughly 64k on the odometer. Rental car runs out Monday, so I need the repair, not homework.

snippets.title: Charge air pipe inspection for lean codes under boost
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. When P0171 sets during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal, inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. A pipe that leaks only under boost admits unmetered air at high load.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Warm AC at idle from an inoperative condenser fan
snippets.text: Applies to models with an electric condenser fan. Vent air may warm up at idle and in traffic and cool again at speed when the condenser fan does not run. With the engine idling and the AC switched on, confirm the condenser fan runs. Without airflow across the condenser at idle, high-side pressure rises. Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2016 compact crossover (2.4L four-cylinder) with 107,182 miles. The AC blows warm from every front vent, driver and passenger side alike. It was cold last summer. snippets.title: Fuel pump relay check for delayed prime
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. If restarts are delayed after towing or extended idling in hot weather, check the fuel pump relay terminals for discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Pressure that rises slowly on a hot restart points to worn relay contacts delaying pump prime.

snippets.title: Rear AC expansion valve check
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2010-2018. When the front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm, compare the front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. A rear outlet line much warmer than the front points to a rear expansion valve stuck closed.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

messages.content: When I stop for 15 to 30 minutes after driving, it cranks at normal speed for five or six seconds before it fires. Cold starts in the morning are instant. Mine is a midsize SUV from 2017, 3.4L V6 under the hood, 77k miles so far. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Repair: replace the purge valve.

snippets.title: CVT fluid and software level check for judder
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. For a judder or shudder during light acceleration from 15-35 mph, check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Degraded fluid or an early software level causes judder at light throttle.

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to all models. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side.

Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core

A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: replace the radiator and flush the cooling system.

snippets.title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for several days because a control module or accessory circuit does not go to sleep. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate the circuit that stays awake by pulling fuses and correct the fault.

snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked.

messages.content: Mine is a small crossover from 2017, 1.4-liter turbo under the hood, 183k miles so far. Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. What's a sensible first test here?
Begin here: after a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V [SM 3.3.7].

Good, that clears this area. Fully charge the battery, let it rest, and run a conductance or load test against the CCA rating on its label [SM 8.3.1].

With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing. Repair: replace the strut upper mounts and bearings.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans (not the 5.5L V8). snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout

Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed.

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing

snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. snippets.title: Dim lights at idle from a slipping accessory belt
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines with a belt-driven alternator, model years 2010-2020. snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software

Revving it makes the light go out. Outside temperature doesn't matter. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans (not the 5.5L V8). snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. messages.content: I have to top off the coolant reservoir every week or two. There are no puddles under the car and it has never overheated. Hi. 2015 compact crossover, 2.4L four-cylinder engine, roughly 168,927 on the odometer.

snippets.title: Wheel speed sensor tone ring inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed.

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
snippets.text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes, model years 2012-2015. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points. Repair: replace the rear drums.

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link.

messages.content: Pedal pulsation when slowing down from highway speed, felt mostly through the steering wheel rather than the seat. No vibration while cruising, and I'm not towing anything. Hi. 2013 minivan, 3.5L V6 engine, roughly 66,844 on the odometer. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor. Some vehicles may set lean codes with high long-term fuel trim at idle because a contaminated sensor element under-reports airflow. With the engine at operating temperature and idling with all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement (about 2-2.5 g/s for a 2.0L engine). Repair: clean the sensor element with an approved cleaner or replace the sensor.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. Some vehicles may set P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

messages.content: Got a 2019 compact sedan here, 2.0L four-cylinder, around 61,258 miles on it. Check engine light is on with P0171 (system too lean, bank 1). The idle is rough, worst for the first few minutes after a cold start. What's a sensible first test here?
With the engine idling, inspect the PCV hose where it joins the intake elbow, flexing it gently while you listen for a vacuum hiss [SEC 17.29]. Write down the reading so we can compare it to spec.
Checked it. The PCV hose at the elbow looks fine, and I can't hear any hiss even when I bend it.

Thanks for checking. With the engine off, smoke-test the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke [SEC 17.6].
The smoke test was clean, nothing leaking at the manifold, throttle body or hoses. Which test makes sense now that this one came back fine?

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. A single-cylinder misfire under load or during acceleration may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with a plug from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

messages.content: Mine is a hatchback from 2017, 1.6L under the hood, 180k miles so far. Misfire code P0302. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. Can you point me to a good starting check?

Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SEC 19.17]. Write down the reading so we can compare it to spec.
Here's what I found. The spark tester showed a solid blue spark the whole time I cranked it.

Good, that clears this area. Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [TSB-2357].
The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain. Nothing showed up, so I'm guessing it's the ignition coil. Agree?

snippets.title: Belt and tensioner check for a battery lamp at cold startup
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. If the battery warning lamp lights for the first minute after a start below 10 deg F, with a short belt squeal that clears once the engine warms, inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. A tensioner that bounces when cold lets the belt slip briefly.

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

messages.content: Hi. 2018 minivan, 3.5-liter V6 engine, roughly 109,251 on the odometer. At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: CVT fluid and software level check for judder
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. For a judder or shudder during light acceleration from 15-35 mph, check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Degraded fluid or an early software level causes judder at light throttle.

snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). Harsh engagements and firm shifts may occur when the pressure control solenoid holds line pressure high. Connect a pressure gauge to the line pressure test port. With the engine idling in drive and the brake applied, line pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

messages.content: Our family's 2011 midsize SUV with the 3.4-liter V6, just past 183,074 miles. Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. Can you skip the testing part and give me the answer?

snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate.
